meta.title: Master Demo — 2026 Consumer Technology, Finance & Digital Lifestyle Study
meta.description: Capability showcase: every question type, display/skip/branch logic, piping, carry-forward, list operations, priority + quota-aware List Fill, four loop kinds with loop-scoped reference columns, a nested loop, randomization, auto-punch, calculations, validation, hidden variables, quotas, custom JavaScript, Conjoint, MaxDiff and a custom design — all connected.

questions.text:
2026 Consumer Technology, Finance & Digital Lifestyle Study

Thank you for taking part. This study asks about the technology you own, the brands you know, how you pay for things and how you feel about digital life. It takes about 20 minutes. Your answers are confidential and reported only in aggregate.

Panel reference: {{ed.PANEL_ID}} · Source: {{ed.SOURCE}}
questions.customHtml:
2026 Consumer Technology, Finance & Digital Lifestyle Study

Thank you for taking part. This study asks about the technology you own, the brands you know, how you pay for things and how you feel about digital life. It takes about 20 minutes. Your answers are confidential and reported only in aggregate.

Panel reference: {{ed.PANEL_ID}} · Source: {{ed.SOURCE}}
questions.notes: [DEMO: Embedded data piping] PANEL_ID and SOURCE are captured from the URL by the embedded_data flow node and piped with {{ed.X}}.

questions.text: Do you agree to participate in this research study?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Termination logic] Skip rule → terminate with status 'screened' when 2 is chosen.

questions.text: Please confirm that you are completing this survey yourself and will answer honestly.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Participation confirmation] Second gate; also demonstrates two terminating rules on one page.

questions.text: How old are you?
questions.instruction: Please enter your age in whole years (18–100).

validation.message: Please enter a whole number of years.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Numeric range validation + termination] minValue/maxValue 18–100, integer rule; under-18 is handled by the schema bound. AGE feeds the AGE_GROUP calculation and the age quotas.

questions.text: Which country do you live in?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Dropdown + other-specify] 'Other country' opens a text field (COUNTRY_other). Drives option-level visibility of REGION.

questions.text: Which region do you live in?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Display logic + option-level visibility] Shown only for 4 countries; each option is visible only for its own country (option.visibleIf).

questions.text: Which city or town do you live in?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Text validation] min_length / max_length.

questions.text: What is your email address?
questions.instruction: Used only to send your incentive.

validation.message: Please enter a valid email address (name@example.com).

questions.notes: [DEMO: Email validation] kind 'email' + the text.email variant.

questions.text: May we contact you about follow-up studies?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Conditional required] Drives PHONE's visibility and its conditional required rule.

questions.text: What phone number may we reach you on?

validation.message: A phone number is required when you agree to be contacted.
Please enter digits, spaces, brackets or dashes only.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Display logic + conditional required + regex] Required only when CONTACT_OK = Yes; pattern validation.

questions.text: Which of these best describes your current employment status?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Skip logic → page] Retired / unemployed / student skip the work-profile page (industry, job level, company size) entirely.

questions.text: Which of the following devices do you personally own or use at least weekly?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Multi-select with 12 options + exclusive 'None' + termination] None terminates (no product ownership). Selected devices drive later display logic (wearables, smart home).

questions.text: When technology is bought in your household, what is your role?

options.label: Someone else decides — I have no say

questions.notes: [DEMO: Screening] No-say respondents are not terminated but are excluded from the pricing block by display logic.

questions.text: Do you use these devices mainly for personal purposes, for work, or both?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Branching driver] The BRANCH node after screening routes Consumer / Business / Both to different blocks using this and EMPLOYMENT together.

questions.text: This is an attention check. Please select “Agree” to continue.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Attention check] Graded by the quality engine; a miss becomes an explained flag, not a termination.

questions.text: How do you describe your gender?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Quota driver] GENDER feeds quota_gender and the Gender × Age combined quota.

questions.text: Including yourself, how many people live in your household?
How many of them are children under 18?

validation.message: Children must be fewer than the total household size.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Cross-question validation] custom_expression compares this answer (`value`) with HH_SIZE.

questions.text: What is your total annual household income before tax?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Display-logic driver] Income ≥ $100k (codes 5–8) unlocks the investment questions in the finance page.

questions.text: What is the highest level of education you have completed?
Which industry do you work in?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Display logic] Shown to employed respondents only (EMPLOYMENT in 1–3).

questions.text: Which best describes your level in your organisation?
Roughly how many people work at your organisation?
questions.notes: [DEMO: AND display logic] Employed AND uses devices for work.

questions.text: When did you buy your most recent technology device?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Date question + date bounds] minDate/maxDate; cross-checked against WARRANTY_END by a custom script.

questions.text: When does its warranty end (your best estimate)?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Cross-question date validation via custom JavaScript] The on_submit script blocks the page when this is before LAST_PURCHASE_DATE.

questions.text: At what time of day do you usually shop online?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Time question]

questions.text: Which of these financial products or services do you currently use?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Multi-select with 13 options] Feeds N_FIN_PRODUCTS calculation and the finance display logic.

questions.text: Derived age group
questions.notes: [DEMO: Hidden derived variable] Text calculation used by the age quotas and the Gender × Age cells.

questions.text: Hidden eligibility flag

settings.expression: if(CONSENT == 1 and PARTICIPATION_OK == 1 and AGE >= 18 and DEVICES_98 == 0, 1, 0)

questions.notes: [DEMO: Hidden eligibility flag] Executes although never displayed — visibility ≠ execution.

questions.text: On a typical day, how many hours do you spend online (excluding work)?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Slider with step and end labels]

questions.text: How often do you do each of the following?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Matrix single-select + row randomization] 8 rows × 6-point frequency scale; rows shuffled per respondent (seeded).

questions.text: Which of these app categories have you used in the past month?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Multi-select dropdown + max selections]

questions.text: Which phone form factor appeals to you most?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Image-based single choice] Inline SVG data URIs so the demo has no external assets.

questions.text: Rank your top 3 priorities when choosing a new device.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Ranking (top-N) + randomized options] Ranked-first condition drives a follow-up open end.

questions.text: How likely are you to recommend your main device to a friend or colleague?
questions.notes: [DEMO: NPS] Feeds the NPS_SEGMENT calculation and a conditional open end.

questions.text: Roughly how much do you spend per month on technology (devices, apps, subscriptions)?
questions.instruction: Enter a whole amount in your local currency.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Numeric currency + piping source] MONTHLY_SPEND is piped inside the brand loop together with loop references (§41).

questions.text: Of that, how much goes on subscriptions (streaming, cloud, software)?

validation.message: Subscriptions cannot exceed your total monthly spend.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Cross-question validation] value ≤ MONTHLY_SPEND.

questions.text: And how much goes on hardware (averaged per month)?

validation.message: Subscriptions plus hardware cannot exceed your total monthly spend.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Cross-question validation] SUB_SPEND + HW_SPEND ≤ MONTHLY_SPEND (the §43 pattern).

questions.text: What percentage of your technology spend goes to each category? (must total 100%)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Allocation / constant sum] sumTarget 100.

questions.text: What percentage of your technology purchases do you make online?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Percentage]

questions.text: Over the past 12 months, roughly how much did you spend on each of the following?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Numeric list] One currency field per row; summed by the TOTAL_SPEND_12M calculation.

questions.text: What is your total technology budget for the next 12 months?

validation.message: Your budget cannot be lower than a year of your current subscriptions.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Logical validation] Compares against a derived value (12 × SUB_SPEND).

questions.text: How satisfied are you with your smartwatch or fitness tracker?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Skip pattern 'no product → skip satisfaction'] Shown only to wearable owners.

questions.text: How satisfied are you with your smart-home setup overall?
questions.notes: [DEMO: OR display logic] Smart speaker OR security camera owners.

questions.text: Which of these investments do you hold?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Nested AND/OR display logic] income ≥ $100k AND (uses investment app OR crypto exchange).

questions.text: Which personal activity matters most to you when choosing technology?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Branch — Consumer path]

questions.text: Which business function do you mainly use technology for?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Branch — Business path]

questions.text: How many devices does your employer provide to you?
How well do your personal and work technology fit together?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Branch — Both path (combined section)]

questions.text: Which technology brands come to mind first? List up to five.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Text list] Unaided awareness; UNAIDED_b1…b5.

questions.text: Which of these technology brands have you heard of?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Multi-select, 12 brands, randomized, exclusive None] The awareness universe for every later brand list.

questions.text: Which of these brands have you personally used in the past 12 months?

mask.label: show only the brands selected in BRANDS_AWARE

questions.notes: [DEMO: Option masking (display only aware brands)] The full brand list is programmed here and masked to the BRANDS_AWARE selection, so the loops over this question know every code they can meet. THIS IS THE LOOP SOURCE for LOOP_001 (selected), LOOP_003 (not selected) and the List Fill.

questions.text: Which 2 to 5 of these brands do you trust the most?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Min/max selection validation + display logic on a calculation] Select 2–5; shown only when N_AWARE ≥ 2.

questions.text: You said you have used {{BRANDS_USED.labels|and}}. Which is your favourite?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Multi-select piping with a format modifier] {{BRANDS_USED.labels|and}} → 'Apple, Google and Samsung'.

questions.text: Why is {{FAV_BRAND}} your favourite?

validation.message: Please tell us a little more (at least 5 characters).

questions.notes: [DEMO: Basic piping + open end] {{FAV_BRAND}} pipes the selected label.

questions.text: How much do you agree that each brand offers good value for money?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Carry-forward into matrix rows] Rows = used brands, 5-point agreement scale. BRAND_AGREE_<code>.

questions.text: Which of these words do you associate with each brand? (select all that apply)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Matrix multi-select] BRAND_ASSOC_<brand>_<attr> 0/1 flags.

questions.text: For how many years have you used each brand?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Matrix numeric + custom-logic 'invalid' detection] A script flags any brand whose years exceed the respondent's AGE — those brands feed LOOP_005 (invalid-item loop).

questions.text: Where did you most recently buy from each brand?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Matrix dropdown]

questions.text: In one word, how would you describe each brand?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Matrix text]

questions.text: Would you be willing to answer a few more detailed questions about the brands you use?

options.label: No, take me to the shorter version

questions.notes: [DEMO: Skip logic → block] 'No' skips the List Fill, list-operation and loop blocks and lands on 11_Loop_Count.

questions.text: Hidden List Fill candidate list (trusted ∩ used, written by script)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Hidden List Fill source] A hidden multi-code question whose answer is set by the 'Build hidden list source' script (used ∩ trusted). LF_TRUST reads it as its candidate list.

questions.text: List Fill destination 1 (allocated brand code)
questions.notes: [DEMO: List Fill destination] Receives position 1 of LF_BRAND_EVAL as its answer.

questions.text: List Fill destination 2 (allocated brand code)
questions.notes: [DEMO: List Fill destination] Position 2; blank when only one item was allocated.

questions.text: Randomly assigned deep-dive topic
questions.notes: [DEMO: Random List Fill destination] LF_TOPIC assigns one of six topics at random (no sample tracking).

questions.text: Thinking about {{LISTFILL_BRAND_EVAL_1}}, how satisfied are you overall?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List Fill piping] {{LISTFILL_BRAND_EVAL_1}} is the label allocated to position 1 (priority → cap → quota → random fallback).

questions.text: And {{LISTFILL_BRAND_EVAL_2}} — how satisfied are you overall?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List Fill count-aware display] Only when two items were allocated (count = min(2, N_BRANDS_USED)).

questions.text: You have been assigned the topic “{{LISTFILL_TOPIC_1}}”. What is the one thing technology brands should improve about {{LISTFILL_TOPIC_1}}?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized List Fill piping] The topic is allocated from a static list with method 'random'.

questions.text: Of the brands you both use and trust, {{LISTFILL_TRUST_1}} was chosen for you. Would you buy from {{LISTFILL_TRUST_1}} again?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List Fill from a hidden source] LF_TRUST's candidates come from the hidden LF_SOURCE_LIST question a script filled.

questions.text: How likely are you to recommend {{loop.label}} ({{loop.Tier}} tier, {{loop.Segment}} segment)?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Loop over List Fill items + loop-scoped references] LOOP_LF iterates the allocated brands; Tier/Segment exist ONLY in LOOP_LF's table — LOOP_001 has different columns for the same brands.

questions.text: What is the main reason for your score for {{loop.label}}?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Open end inside a List Fill loop]

questions.text: Of the brands you know but have not used, which are you most curious about?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List operation — DIFFERENCE] The full brand universe is programmed, then the pipeline keeps aware(selected) − used(selected). Shown only when the result is non-empty (N_AWARE_NOT_USED ≥ 1).

questions.text: Which of these brands would you consider for your next purchase?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List operation — UNION + DEDUPE] used ∪ trusted, duplicates removed.

questions.text: Which of the brands you both use and trust would you call your core brand?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List operation — INTERSECT] used ∩ trusted.

questions.text: Which of these brands had you never heard of before today?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List operation — REMAINING] Keeps the brands that appear in no source list — here, everything the respondent did not tick in BRANDS_AWARE.

questions.text: From this alphabetical list of the brands you use, which has the best customer service?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Ordered list] settings.optionOrder = 'az' sorts the carried list; the programmed order is never modified.

questions.text: Of these three brands (chosen at random from those you know), which would you research first?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized list — pick N] Shuffle and present only 3 of the aware brands.

questions.text: Which of these brands would you recommend to a friend?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Nested set expression (mask)] (used ∪ consider) ∩ aware — brackets the sequential pipeline cannot express.

questions.text: Which brand would you buy from tomorrow?
questions.notes: [DEMO: List logic — PRIORITIZE] The favourite brand floats to the top of the carried list.

questions.text: How familiar are you with {{CURRENT_ITEM}}?
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_001 — CURRENT_ITEM piping] Repeats once per brand selected in BRANDS_USED; answers export as L1_FAMILIAR_1…N with LOOP_BRAND_ITEM_n_CODE as the join key.

questions.text: How frequently do you use {{CURRENT_ITEM}} products or services? (brand {{LOOP_INDEX}} of {{LOOP_COUNT}})
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_INDEX / LOOP_COUNT piping]

questions.text: Please rate {{CURRENT_ITEM.Brand_Nickname}}, product {{CURRENT_ITEM.Product_ID}}, in the {{CURRENT_ITEM.Category}} category.
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP REFERENCES — several columns in one sentence] Brand_Nickname, Product_ID and Category are read from LOOP_001's own reference table.

questions.text: Why do you use {{CURRENT_ITEM}}?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Open end inside a loop] Exported per iteration.

questions.text: How likely are you to buy from {{CURRENT_ITEM}} again?
As a {{CURRENT_ITEM.Product_Type}} company headquartered in {{CURRENT_ITEM.Region}}, how does {{CURRENT_ITEM}} perform on…
questions.notes: [DEMO: References Product_Type + Region in question text; matrix inside a loop]

questions.text: How satisfied are you with the software updates on your {{CURRENT_ITEM}} smartphone?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Display logic on a loop reference] loop.Category = 'Smartphone' — only smartphone brands see this iteration question.

questions.text: Earlier you said you spend about {{MONTHLY_SPEND}} per month on technology. Given that, how good value is {{CURRENT_ITEM.Brand_Nickname}} (product {{CURRENT_ITEM.Product_ID}}) — and how does it compare with your favourite, {{FAV_BRAND}}?
questions.notes: [DEMO §41: Question piping + loop piping + calculated/previous answer in one text] MONTHLY_SPEND (earlier answer), CURRENT_ITEM.* (loop references), FAV_BRAND (earlier answer).

questions.text: Would you recommend {{CURRENT_ITEM}} to a friend?
Category classification for {{CURRENT_ITEM}} (auto-populated from the loop's reference data — read only)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Auto-punch from loop context / reference values + read-only field] Three punch rules keyed on loop.Category; the respondent sees the result but cannot change it.

questions.text: Rate {{brand.label}} on {{feature.label}} ({{feature.Feature_Group}} group).
questions.notes: [DEMO: NESTED LOOP piping] {{brand.label}} = outer item, {{feature.label}} = inner item, {{feature.Feature_Group}} = inner loop's reference. Exports as L2_FEATURE_<outer>_<inner>.

questions.text: Is {{loop.label}} a reason you chose {{brand.Brand_Nickname}}?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Nested loop — innermost via {{loop.*}}, outer via its loopVar] References of the outer loop (Brand_Nickname) and inner loop do not collide.

questions.text: Why haven't you used {{CURRENT_ITEM}} in the past year?

options.label: Not compatible with my other devices

questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_003 — FOR EACH NOT-SELECTED brand] Source filter 'notSelected' on BRANDS_USED (aware but not used); at most 3 iterations in random order.

questions.text: How likely are you to try {{CURRENT_ITEM}} in the next 12 months?
{{loop.Reason_Prompt}}
questions.notes: [DEMO: A whole question text from a reference column] LOOP_003's table carries a per-brand prompt (Reason_Prompt).

questions.text: {{CURRENT_ITEM}} has stopped selling consumer devices in several markets since {{loop.Exit_Year}}. Were you aware of this?
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_004 — filter 'invalid'] Items are invalid when LOOP_004's invalidIf holds: loop.Market_Status = 'exited' (its own reference column). Here that marks Huawei and LG.

questions.text: Does that change how you feel about {{CURRENT_ITEM}}?
You entered {{loop.label}} years for {{loop.Brand}}, which is more than your age ({{AGE}}). Please re-enter the number of years you have used {{loop.Brand}}.
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_005 — invalid items defined by custom logic] The years-used script writes INVALID_BRANDS as [{code, label: years}]; the loop source is that variable ({{loop.label}} = years entered) and the loop's own reference table supplies the Brand name.

questions.text: How many individual technology products would you like to tell us about in detail? (1–5)
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_006 — FOR i = 1 TO N_PRODUCTS] The loop's source is {kind:'count', count:{kind:'question', ref:'q_n_products'}}: answering 5 runs the block five times.

questions.text: Product {{LOOP_INDEX}} of {{LOOP_COUNT}}: what type of product is it?
questions.notes: [DEMO: LOOP_INDEX in a count loop]

questions.text: What is the brand and model of product {{LOOP_INDEX}}?
Roughly how much did product {{LOOP_INDEX}} cost?
How satisfied are you with product {{LOOP_INDEX}}?
Which of these features do you use on your phone at least weekly?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized options with anchors] 10 shuffled options; None/Other anchored to the bottom.

questions.text: Which of these payment methods do you use most often?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Rotation] method 'rotate' — order preserved, start point varies per respondent.

questions.text: How much do you agree with each statement?

rows.label: Technology makes my daily life easier
I worry about how companies use my data
I prefer to pay for products outright rather than subscribe
I trust digital banks as much as traditional banks
I upgrade my devices as soon as a new model is released
Sustainability influences which brands I buy

questions.notes: [DEMO: reverse_half] Half the sample sees the statements in reverse order.

questions.text: Which of these five features would you pay extra for?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomize N from a list] pick 5 of 12.

questions.text: Which streaming service would you keep if you could keep only one?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Conditional randomization] Options shuffle only for respondents under 35; everyone else sees the programmed order.

questions.text: Which of these best describes your attitude to new technology?

options.label: I buy when there's no choice

questions.notes: [DEMO: Grouped randomization] Shuffle within groups; groups stay in place.

questions.text: Please read the following message.

arms.label: Rational message
arms.html: Save $240 a year by switching to a mid-range phone with three years of guaranteed updates.

arms.label: Emotional message
arms.html: Keep the phone you love, longer. Three years of updates means three years of feeling at home.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized experiment arms] Each respondent is assigned A or B (seeded); MESSAGE_ARM stores the arm and drives the next question's piping and display.

questions.text: How convincing did you find the message you just read?
How concerned are you about how technology companies use your personal data?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized block A] One of three blocks shown in random order (2 of 3).

questions.text: How important is a brand's environmental record when you buy technology?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized block B]

questions.text: How comfortable are you with AI features in your everyday devices?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Randomized block C]

questions.text: Here is a summary of what you told us (calculated, read only).
questions.notes: [DEMO: Read-only calculated fields] Every column has an `expression`; the cells are computed live and are never editable.

questions.text: Your total technology spend over the last 12 months works out to about {{calc.TOTAL_SPEND_12M}}, and your average brand rating is {{calc.AVG_BRAND_RATING}} out of 100. Does that look right?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Calculated-variable piping] {{calc.TOTAL_SPEND_12M}} and {{calc.AVG_BRAND_RATING}} come from the calculations list.

questions.text: What should the 12-month total be?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Conditional required] Required only when the respondent disagreed with the calculation.

questions.text: Based on your answers we would describe you as a “{{calc.TECH_SEGMENT}}” (engagement score {{calc.ENGAGEMENT_SCORE}}/100). Does that feel accurate?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Weighted score + text segment] ENGAGEMENT_SCORE is a weighted() calculation; TECH_SEGMENT is an if() chain over it.

questions.text: Spend segment (auto-populated, read only)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Auto-punch from a previous numeric answer] Three punch rules with `when` conditions on MONTHLY_SPEND.

questions.text: Favourite brand (auto-populated from your earlier answer)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Auto-punch by reference] The favourite brand's code is copied into this question (same codes, no mapping).

questions.text: Ecosystem (auto-populated with a mapped value)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Auto-punch with a mapping] FAV_BRAND code → ecosystem code (Apple → ios, Samsung → android, …).

questions.text: Allocated evaluation brand (auto-populated from List Fill)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Auto-punch from a List Fill result] Reads the hidden destination LF_BRAND_1.

questions.text: Heavy digital user (auto-populated from a calculation)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Auto-punch from a calculation] when ENGAGEMENT_SCORE ≥ 60.

questions.text: Select exactly three concerns you have about technology.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Exact selection count] minSelections = maxSelections = 3.

questions.text: What is your postal / ZIP code?

validation.message: Please enter a valid postal code (3–10 letters/digits).

questions.notes: [DEMO: Regex validation]

questions.text: How many connected devices are in your home in total?

validation.message: This cannot be lower than the number of device types you selected earlier.

questions.notes: [DEMO: Logical validation against a count()] value ≥ count(DEVICES).

questions.text: In a few words, what is the best thing about your main device?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Text length validation]

questions.text: When do you plan your next upgrade window?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Multi-column date pair + custom JavaScript validation] The on_submit script rejects To < From.

questions.text: Sample cell (auto-populated from gender × age, read only)
questions.notes: [DEMO: Quota flag as a visible read-only variable] Mirrors the Gender × Age quota cells so testers can see which cell they fell into. The quotas themselves are enforced by the quota_check node after demographics.

questions.text: Hidden quota flag
questions.notes: [DEMO: Hidden quota flag] Text key of the combined quota cell, e.g. 1_25-34.

questions.text: Hidden score
questions.notes: [DEMO: Hidden score] Mean of the loop ratings L1_SAT_1…N (positional loop variables).

questions.text: Hidden loop control
questions.notes: [DEMO: Hidden loop control] LOOP_001 uses count.mode 'max' with this calculation, so at most 6 brands are evaluated even if more were used.

questions.text: Next you will see 9 sets of three smartphone offers. In each set, choose the one you would buy — or none of them.
questions.customHtml: Next you will see 9 sets of three smartphone offers. In each set, choose the one you would buy — or none of them.

questions.text: Which of these would you choose?
questions.notes: [DEMO: CONJOINT] Renders the tasks of design 'design_conjoint_phone' (4 attributes, 3 alternatives + None, 8 tasks + 1 holdout, 2 versions, seed 20260901). Shown only to decision-makers (PURCHASE_ROLE 1–2).

questions.text: Which single attribute mattered most in the choices you just made?
Why did {{CBC_DRIVER}} matter most?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Piping a single-select label into an open end]

questions.text: For each set, pick the feature that matters MOST and the one that matters LEAST when buying a phone.
questions.notes: [DEMO: MAXDIFF] 12 items, 5 per task, 9 tasks, 2 versions (design_maxdiff_features, seed 20260902).

questions.text: Overall, rank the three features that matter most to you.
questions.notes: [DEMO: MaxDiff follow-up with the same item list]

questions.text: Statement: “{{loop.Statement}}” ({{loop.Component}} · intensity level {{loop.Level}}). How much do you agree?
questions.notes: [DEMO: CUSTOM DESIGN loop] LOOP_007 iterates the rows of design_custom_statements; the statement text, component and level are carried as LOOP_007 references keyed by task number.

questions.text: Why do you feel that way about “{{loop.Statement}}”?
questions.notes: [DEMO: Display logic on a numeric loop reference] Only for level-3 statements.

questions.text: For each product you own, tell us a bit more.
questions.notes: [DEMO §40: Complex multi-column question] One logical question, five response types (single / multi / dropdown / text / numeric), each column its own variable stem and validation; rows shown only for owned devices.

questions.text: Split 100% of your weekly screen time across devices, for weekdays and weekends.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Constant-sum grid] Each row must total 100 (settings.rowSum + sumTarget).

questions.text: List the paid digital subscriptions you have (add as many as apply).
questions.notes: [DEMO: Repeating group] Respondent-driven repetition (1–8 entries).

questions.text: Click the area of this device that you touch most often.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Hotspot] Stores click coordinates HOTSPOT_1_X/Y.

questions.text: Mark anything you would change about this concept design (pin + comment, or draw).
questions.notes: [DEMO: Annotation] Pins and strokes on a stimulus image.

questions.text: Rank these colour finishes from most to least appealing.
questions.notes: [DEMO: Image ranking]

questions.text: Optionally, upload a photo or screenshot of your most recent technology receipt.
